arguments.command:
python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# Treasury data (in millions of dollars)
Europe_1991 = 268166
Latin_America_1991 = 337565
Europe_1996 = 426245
Latin_America_1996 = 443872

# Germany's nominal GDP (World Bank data, in billions of dollars)
# 1991: 1875792575132.59 -> 1875.79 billion
# 1996: 2506576553158.31 -> 2506.58 billion
Germany_GDP_1991 = 1875.79
Germany_GDP_1996 = 2506.58

print("="*60)
print("STEP 1: Treasury Data")
print("="*60)
print(f"June 1991 - Europe: {Europe_1991:,} million")
print(f"June 1991 - Latin America & Caribbean: {Latin_America_1991:,} million")
print(f"June 1996 - Europe: {Europe_1996:,} million")
print(f"June 1996 - Latin America & Caribbean: {Latin_America_1996:,} million")

print("\n" + "="*60)
print("STEP 2: Linear Regression (Europe as predictor of Latin America)")
print("="*60)

# With 2 points, linear regression passes through both
# Slope = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)
slope = (Latin_America_1996 - Latin_America_1991) / (Europe_1996 - Europe_1991)
print(f"Slope: {slope:.6f}")

# Intercept = y - mx
intercept = Latin_America_1991 - slope * Europe_1991
print(f"Intercept: {intercept:.2f}")

# Regression equation
print(f"Regression: Latin America = {slope:.6f} * Europe + {intercept:.2f}")

print("\n" + "="*60)
print("STEP 3: Germany's GDP Growth Rate")
print("="*60)
print(f"Germany GDP 1991: ${Germany_GDP_1991:.2f} billion")
print(f"Germany GDP 1996: ${Germany_GDP_1996:.2f} billion")

germany_growth_rate = (Germany_GDP_1996 - Germany_GDP_1991) / Germany_GDP_1991 * 100
print(f"Germany growth rate: {germany_growth_rate:.4f}%")

print("\n" + "="*60)
print("STEP 4: Counterfactual Europe value")
print("="*60)
# Apply Germany's growth rate to June 1991 Europe value
counterfactual_europe_1996 = Europe_1991 * (1 + germany_growth_rate/100)
print(f"Counterfactual Europe (1996): {counterfactual_europe_1996:.2f} million")

print("\n" + "="*60)
print("STEP 5: Predict Latin America using regression")
print("="*60)
predicted_latin_america = slope * counterfactual_europe_1996 + intercept
print(f"Predicted Latin America: {predicted_latin_america:.2f} million")

print("\n" + "="*60)
print("STEP 6: Calculate absolute difference and percentage")
print("="*60)
absolute_difference = abs(predicted_latin_america - Latin_America_1996)
print(f"Actual Latin America 1996: {Latin_America_1996:,} million")
print(f"Predicted Latin America: {predicted_latin_america:,.2f} million")
print(f"Absolute difference: {absolute_difference:,.2f} million")

percentage_of_actual = (absolute_difference / Latin_America_1996) * 100
print(f"Percentage of actual: {percentage_of_actual:.4f}%")

print("\n" + "="*60)
print("STEP 7: Calculate U.S. liabilities growth ratio")
print("="*60)
us_liabilities_1991 = Europe_1991 + Latin_America_1991
us_liabilities_1996 = Europe_1996 + Latin_America_1996
print(f"US Liabilities 1991 (Europe + Latin America): {us_liabilities_1991:,} million")
print(f"US Liabilities 1996 (Europe + Latin America): {us_liabilities_1996:,} million")

us_liabilities_growth = (us_liabilities_1996 - us_liabilities_1991) / us_liabilities_1991 * 100
print(f"US Liabilities growth rate: {us_liabilities_growth:.4f}%")

# Germany GDP growth as a ratio (not percentage)
germany_gdp_growth_ratio = Germany_GDP_1996 / Germany_GDP_1991
print(f"Germany GDP growth ratio: {germany_gdp_growth_ratio:.6f}")

us_liabilities_growth_ratio = us_liabilities_1996 / us_liabilities_1991
print(f"US Liabilities growth ratio: {us_liabilities_growth_ratio:.6f}")

ratio_us_liab_to_germany_gdp = us_liabilities_growth_ratio / germany_gdp_growth_ratio
print(f"Ratio (US liabilities growth / Germany GDP growth): {ratio_us_liab_to_germany_gdp:.6f}")

print("\n" + "="*60)
print("STEP 8: Final calculation")
print("="*60)
final_result = percentage_of_actual * ratio_us_liab_to_germany_gdp
print(f"Final result: {percentage_of_actual:.4f} * {ratio_us_liab_to_germany_gdp:.6f}")
print(f"Final result (rounded to 2 decimal places): {final_result:.2f}")

# Store for output
print(f"\n>>> FINAL ANSWER: {final_result:.2f}")
EOF

EOF
